tw-wi-portage-pauquette-kegs.st: The 1880 county history says he was shot on Monday 17 October 1836 by Man-ze-mon-e-ka, son of Whirling Thunder, after a quarrel at a treaty council near the portage and Paul Grignon's house. At his death he held 'twelve or sixteen sections of land, a large number of cattle and horses', and the fur company collected $22,000 owed him (1838), but 'all this property disappeared without the heirs receiving a cent'. That vanished estate is the likely kernel the kegs legend grew on; the 1865 guardianship sale notice fits. He was buried under his unfinished log church near the centre of Portage and reburied in 1852 beneath the threshold of the south entrance of the Catholic church at Conant and Adams Streets; he also had a farm at 'Belle Fontaine'.
src: Butterfield, History of Columbia County, Wisconsin (1880), Pauquette sketch
